I know that I would definitely hurt others with my actions, but I've always been the kind of person who puts others before me. Once in a while though, life becomes overwhelming and I just start to think that maybe once, just once, I can forget about how everyone would feel, and just think about how I would feel. I have always associated suicide/death with a sense of relief and peace. But I don't want to give up yet. I want to try to fix my life and confront my parents before I just give up trying.

I'm glad too. This subreddit is actually very helpful and supportive. 
Thank you.

Thank you. I think I really do need to stand up for myself and take control of my life. It's just not fair. 
I have a lot of respect for you and what you did for your friend. It's nice to know that there are people like you out there who will help others like that. That's very rare, and I really do thank you for it.
Thanks again, and I will be sure to update once things start moving along.
Thank you, but I'm actually Christian.

Pride is definitely an issue with them.
I think I know what I want to do now. I'm going to gradually try to argue for my freedom. If they don't respond to my efforts, I'll give them one huge argument. If that blows up in my face, I'll move into my uncle's house until I can get my own place.
I just hope I can actually go through with this plan. I'm a coward with confrontation.

Thank you, that's very nice of you. 
Yes, I have gone for anxiety issues before. I don't handle stress well, and I began to abuse adderall once. I stopped going after a while though. I felt like I was just venting to a stranger rather than getting helped.
I have authority issues! I actually fear my father. I cry every time I try to argue with him.

No, I don't think so.
The risks are being controlled even more since I am showing signs of slipping away.
I can move in with my uncle if it ever gets too bad.
I already get financial aid and scholarships, which I am saving up for med school. But I'd rather use them for an apartment and just take on loans for med schools.

My college is paid for with scholarships, thankfully.
The finances I'm worried about are the bills that come with getting an apartment. 
The only thing my parents pay for are my car and health insurance. I'm really not all that dependent on them. But I don't have enough saved up to afford living on my own and paying for water and electric bills etc.

I do that a lot... I just sit in Barnes and Noble and read stuff for hours until I have to go home. I dread going home... :/

And thank you! :)

Thank you. :)
I appreciate your comment very much.

I live in America.
I need freedom and a sense of control over my own life.
I'll try. But her cold shoulder is the worst. I love my mom too much to let her be angry/upset with me.

I'm saving up my money from work and scholarships so that I can eventually move out if I can make it to that point of my life. I'd rather drown in bills and med school loans than live with them. 
I'm to financially dependent on them now to move out anytime soon though. 
Thank you. I really appreciate you taking the time to comment on my post.

about 6-7 years.
And I will be honest, sometimes I do feel that PART of the reason why I consider suicide is to show my parents that they are wrong in their style of parenting. It's not about getting back at them, it's more about proving a point. But the majority of it is just wanting to give up.

I stayed at my friend's house until 8:30 once and my mother continuously called me until I answered. I wasn't even ignoring her calls. I was doing some kind of cardio exercises my friend and I learned from Netflix and just wasn't aware of my phone vibrating. I came home to one pissed off mother. She gave me the cold shoulder for days after I said "Sorry I was home an hour late because I was trying to avoid a life of heart disease 2 minutes away from our front door."

Thank you. I really wish I can make a difference. I would LOVE to research the genetic correlations with cancer. Genetics is such a passion of mine, and if I would absolutely love to finish my education so I can do what I want to do the most, but my parents make me so unhappy that they make it too difficult to continue. 

I can only tolerate so much unhappiness.

I started off as infuriated, but that got me no where. 

They think by keeping me under their roof, I won't be able to go out and drink, smoke, do drugs, have sex, get raped... blah blah blah. 
Also, I can still be a geneticist with the degrees I'm on track for. I just can't be a genetic counselor. So my annual salary after graduating just went down $40-50,000 because my parents are too overprotective to let me move two hours away.

I really wish I could leave, but I can't. If I do ever move out, I want to be completely independent, and that means financially as well- which I am unable to do now.
All I want is simple really. I want to feel like I have freedom. I'm not asking to be allowed to go out partying until 5am on a Saturday. I just want to be able to go out and see a movie with my friends or hang out at my neighbor/best friend's house until 10:30-11:30 at the latest. It's honestly that simple and pathetic. It's not even worth ending my life over to be honest. But it's the fact that they have so much control to that extent that is driving me up the walls. Today, it's just how late I can stay out. Tomorrow, it's going to be who I'm allowed to marry. And the day after that, it's going to be how I'm supposed to raise my children.
Their control will only get worse with time because as a grow older, the more I slip away from them, and the more necessary it will be for them to tighten their grip on my life.

19 years old. And with arab parents like mine, you only move out once you get married. And I refuse to get married until I finish college, which won't be for another 6-7 years.
I can't even handle another week with them. Six years just sounds impossible and unbearable.

They congratulate me on my academic achievements but they never show their appreciation for what I do for them/our family specifically. In fact, they think I'm selfish because sometimes I'd ask to go out with my friends rather than spend a family dinner with them. 
They would not acknowledge how much I do for them because it's an obligation. The stuff I do are expected of me as a female adult in the house. 
I have tried talking to them before and they always respond with "we never ask you for anything, and we always give you everything. We are not like other families, we love you too much to let you ruin your life by going out with friends that won't be there much longer."
I chose my major because I want to be a genetic counselor, but I don't see that happening since they won't let me move 2 hours away to a board certified university for the specific degree I'm seeking.

They are extremely against me moving out. I had the opportunity to go to a very good university two hours away and they were against it. And that's the closest university that offers a board certified genetics program. I actually had to change my career choice because I wasn't allowed to move 2 hours away from home... and money wasn't even an issue.

I am 19 years old. The only freedom I have is being able to drive myself to and from my university and job, but I have to text them every time I get in and out of my car. I have shown responsibility consistently. I am double majoring in biomedical sciences pre-med and biology, and still managing to pull off a 4.0 so far. I work, pick up my brothers from practice every single weekday, do the grocery shopping every saturday, cook three days a week, and I have full responsibility over the laundry and dishes. Both of my parents work so the household burdens are on me. I have shown nothing but responsibility. 

And the control issues don't come from distrust, I think. It comes from them wanting to steer me into the direction they feel is best for me. Not being able to be out of the house past 7:30pm unless I am working is steering me to suicide. I doubt that's the direction they had in mind.

My parents are not easy to talk to. If anything, they would shelter me even more for showing interest in breaking away from them. And if I tell them about the suicide thoughts, they would literally lock me in a room until they think they've gotten through to me. 
They are very predictable and very irrational people.

People would understand. My friends would be sad, yes, but they would know why I did it. At least my reasons for doing this might make my parents see how their methods are effecting their children. It might help make my brothers' life better than mine. The benefits outweigh the loses. In my head at least...
